capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction and use the standard pullback characterizations.

- For the first part, cancel the monomorphism \(f\) in the pullback relation to obtain \(t.\mathrm{fst}=t.\mathrm{snd}\). The diagonal cone on \(X\), with both legs \(\mathrm{id}_X\), induces a map \(X\to t.pt\). One inverse identity follows directly from the lifting equations; the other follows by pullback hom-extensionality, using equality of the two projections. Thus \(t.\mathrm{fst}\) is an isomorphism. Monicity is the essential cancellation mechanism.

- For the second part, use the characterization of `CoproductDisjoint X` relative to a chosen colimit cofan. The witness `hc` identifies `c` as the coproduct, and the typeclass hypothesis supplies monicity of every coproduct injection. For distinct \(i,j\), take `s hij` as the pullback model: `hs hij` proves it is the pullback of the two injections, while `H hij` says its apex is initial. These are exactly the pairwise-disjointness conditions. If the characterization is phrased independently of the chosen cofan, transport them along the unique isomorphism between colimit cofans.
